newsitem.title: USA: MOTOR RACING-ZANARDI TOP QUALIFIER FOR MIAMI INDYCAR RACE.
newsitem.headline: MOTOR RACING-ZANARDI TOP QUALIFIER FOR MIAMI INDYCAR RACE.

text.p: Italy's Alessandro
Zanardi outdueled Brazil's Mauricio Gugelmin for the pole and
another Brazilian, Gil de Ferran, walked away from a
high-speed crash Saturday in qualifying for Sunday's CART
IndyCar series opener.
Speeding around the 1.517-mile (2.441 km) oval with a lap
of 28 seconds flat, Zanardi tied a record of five consecutive
poles, sharing the mark with Bobby Unser and Bobby Rahal and
broke a record with his ninth consecutive front-row starts.
The 30-year-old ex-Formula One driver earned his seventh
IndyCar pole at an average speed of 195.043 mph (313.883 kph).
Gugelmin, also a former Formula One driver, equalled his
best qualifying effort in a Reynard Mercedes-Benz only 25
thousandths of a second behind the pole sitter at 28.025
seconds.
On de Ferran's second of two hot qualifying laps, after
turning a time of 28.050 that was good enough for third on the
grid in a Reynard Honda, his car went out of control.
"The engine misfired for a moment going into turn one. I
don't know if it had anything to do with the accident or not.
The car took off right from the turn and headed for the wall.
It became a case of damage limitation, not avoidance."
De Ferran was able to control the car to some degree,
swerving to only graze the wall rather than hit it at a sharp
angle and reducing his speed from the 190 mph (305 kph) range
to about 150 mph (240 kph).
Thanks to a new padded cockpit rule, he had no physical
after-effects. "Normally in this type of crash you have a
severe headache and ringing ears afterward. In the case I fell
totally fine."
Twenty-eight drivers qualified for the 150-lap, 225-mile
(362 km) race.
